docs.title: ERDIF
docs.text:
European Real Estate Data Interchange Format — an open data format for exchanging real estate listings between systems across Europe.

Beta

This specification is a beta. The data model may still change before version 1.0; see Versioning.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Real estate portals, agency software and aggregators exchange listings in proprietary, country-specific formats. Every integration means a new mapping, and concepts that differ between countries — layout notation, national address registries, local price conventions — are hard to compare.

ERDIF defines one vocabulary and one serialization for a listing that:

  • has a common international core (property type, transaction type, price with currency, area in m², coordinates) understandable in any country,
  • identifies the location through European INSPIRE identifiers with WGS 84 coordinates as a mandatory fallback,
  • carries human-readable text in any number of languages,
  • gives every attribute a machine-readable meaning through links to public vocabularies,
  • separates personal data of the contact so it can be removed independently,
  • is independent of the transport interface — it describes the document, not the API that carries it.

It is intended for developers of systems that export or import listings: portals, agency CRMs, aggregators and search engines.

docs.title: Core principles
docs.text:
• Serialized as JSON-LD 1.1, so a document is plain JSON for developers and linked data for machines
  • schema.org as the default vocabulary (@vocab)
  • Custom erdif: namespace for European specifics
  • Entities carry multiple types (e.g. RealEstateListing + erdif:Advert)
  • Codelist values are dereferenceable IRIs in the erdif-cl: namespace
  • Human-readable text is stored as language maps

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Data model of 15 classes: the root Advert with Price, Contact, Media and ExportInformation; Realty with Building, Room, Equipment, UtilityNetwork, Parking and LocalArea; Location with InspireIdentifier and LocalIdentifier
  • Three-level geolocation: INSPIRE identifier, mandatory WGS 84 coordinates with an explicit approximateCoordinates flag, and national identifiers with a postal address
  • Namespaces erdif: (https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1#) and erdif-cl: (https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/codelist/v1/)
  • JSON-LD 1.1 context schema/context.jsonld declaring every term explicitly, with XSD datatype coercions, codelist values expanding to erdif-cl: IRIs, and @protected
  • Term registry schema/terms/ with the properties, ranges, cardinalities and cross-property validation rules of every class
  • JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for every class in schema/
  • RDFS/OWL vocabulary docs/ns/v1/erdif.ttl (Turtle) generated from the term registry and the codelists, for linked-data tooling such as Dataspecer
  • 16 codelists, all open until 1.0: TransactionType, RealtyType, OwnershipType, EnergyClass, RealtyCondition, ConstructionType, RoomType, EquipmentType, AccessibilityFeature, UtilityNetwork, UtilityConnection, ParkingType, PriceType, ContactType, MediaType, AmenityType; appliesTo restricts where a value may be used
  • Human-readable text as language maps
  • Documentation: data model, namespaces, codelists, localization, geolocation, versioning and conformance
  • Example documents: an apartment for sale and a house for rent, and four invalid documents, each breaking exactly one rule

docs.title: Codelists
docs.text: The source of truth is the codelists/ directory. The codelist pages are generated from it on every docs build.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Value identifiers are English, in PascalCase
  • Values are not translated — labels only serve as documentation
  • Labels and descriptions are language maps; a column is shown for every language present in the data
  • appliesTo on a value restricts where it may be used — the level (Realty, Room) for accessibility features, or the network for utility connections
  • During JSON-LD expansion a value resolves to the IRI https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/codelist/v1/<Codelist>#<Code>

docs.title: Open and closed codelists
docs.text:
• Closed (closed: true) — the list is exhaustive; the producer must use one of the listed values and validation may reject unknown values.
  • Open (closed: false) — the list is representative; the producer may use its own code and validation must accept it.

Development version

Until version 1.0 all codelists are open. Which codelists become closed will be decided before the release.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 when they appear in bold.

docs.title: Conforming document
docs.text:
A document conforms to ERDIF v1 when all of the following hold:

  1. It is valid JSON encoded in UTF-8.
  2. Its @context is the ERDIF context (https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1/context.jsonld), and it is valid JSON-LD 1.1.
  3. Its root is an Advert whose formatVersion is a v1 version of this specification (see Versioning).
  4. Every entity carries the erdif: type of its class, as described in the multiple typing rule.
  5. Every property satisfies the range and cardinality given in its class's property table.
  6. Every entity satisfies the validation rules of its class.
  7. Every codelist value is either listed in the codelist, or the codelist is open (see Codelists).
  8. Values follow the referenced standards: language map keys are ISO 639-1 codes, currencies are ISO 4217 codes, units are UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 codes, coordinates are WGS 84, country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 and date-times are ISO 8601 with a time zone.

The examples in examples/valid/ conform; each document in examples/invalid/ breaks exactly one of the rules above and explains which one in its _comment.

docs.title: Validation with JSON Schema
docs.text:
The JSON Schemas in schema/ check a document in its compact form, starting from advert.schema.json. They cover conditions 3–8 above, except for:

  • the validation rules renovation-after-construction (JSON Schema cannot compare two values) and parking-price (a recommendation spanning two entities),
  • the informative rules advert-id-vs-source-id and amenity-schema-type, which state no constraint,
  • the codes of condition 8 (currency, unit, country, language), which are checked by their shape only, not against the official code lists.

Condition 2 — valid JSON-LD 1.1 — needs a JSON-LD processor. Validators must enable format assertion (e-mail, URI and date-time checks); the time zone of date-times is enforced by a pattern either way.

The schemas accept properties they do not know, so a document of a newer minor version stays valid against an older schema (see Versioning).

docs.title: Producers
docs.text:
A system that exports ERDIF documents:

  • MUST produce conforming documents,
  • MUST state approximateCoordinates truthfully,
  • SHOULD use the most specific schema.org type available,
  • SHOULD provide description in the language of the market and in English,
  • SHOULD use a listed codelist value whenever one fits, and a custom code only when none does,
  • MUST NOT put personal data anywhere other than in Contact.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
A system that imports ERDIF documents:

  • MUST reject documents whose major version it does not support,
  • MUST accept unknown codes in open codelists,
  • SHOULD ignore properties it does not know instead of rejecting the document,
  • SHOULD use exportInformation (sourceSystem + sourceAdvertId) to match repeated imports of the same advert,
  • SHOULD preserve localIdentifiers unchanged when passing data on,
  • MUST be able to delete or anonymise a Contact independently of the rest of the advert.

docs.title: Invalid documents
docs.text:
Each invalid example breaks exactly one rule. _comment explains which one, and _expect states the error a JSON Schema validator reports — the JSON Pointer of the failing value and the failing keyword. They are meant as test cases for importers.

Example Broken rule Expected error missing-gps-fallback.jsonld geo is required on Location /realty/location — required price-without-amount.jsonld price-or-on-request /prices/0 — anyOf room-feature-on-realty.jsonld accessibility-level /realty/accessibility/0 — not land-with-rooms.jsonld land-has-no-rooms /realty/rooms — maxItems

All examples are checked in CI by scripts/validate_examples.py: valid documents must pass the schema and expand as JSON-LD, invalid ones must fail with exactly the expected error and no other.

docs.title: Geolocation
docs.text: ERDIF identifies the location of a property through a three-level hierarchy. Each level has a different role; together they guarantee that a property can always be shown on a map and, where possible, linked to authoritative spatial data. All levels live in Location.

docs.title: 1. INSPIRE identifier
docs.text:
The primary, supranational reference. The EU INSPIRE directive obliges member states to publish spatial data with a common structure, so an INSPIRE identifier works the same way in every country. It resolves to the spatial object itself — including its geometry — and through it to the national address.

ERDIF uses three INSPIRE themes:

Theme Spatial object Typical use AD Address point Apartments, houses BU Building Whole buildings CP Cadastral parcel Land, properties without address 
"globalIdentifier": {
  "@type": "erdif:InspireIdentifier",
  "theme": "AD",
  "namespace": "CZ.CUZK.AD",
  "localId": "26777598"
}

The identifier is optional, because it may not exist yet — typically for new buildings that are not registered.

docs.title: 2. GPS coordinates (WGS 84)
docs.text:
A mandatory fallback that must always be present, given in WGS 84. It guarantees that every property can at least be shown as a point on a map, even when no INSPIRE identifier is available.

"geo": {
  "@type": "GeoCoordinates",
  "latitude": 50.07553,
  "longitude": 14.43781
},
"approximateCoordinates": false

Many advertisers deliberately shift the point to hide the exact address. approximateCoordinates states whether that is the case, and must always be given explicitly:

  • false — the point marks the property; it can be used for precise map display and distance calculations,
  • true — the point is only approximate; consumers should show an area rather than a pin.

docs.title: 3. National identifiers
docs.text:
Supplementary metadata: identifiers from national registries (for example RÚIAN in the Czech Republic) and the postal address in the local format. They have no system role at the European level — ERDIF does not use them to locate the property — but they are passed through unchanged so that the end user or a local system can verify the property in the national registry.

"localIdentifiers": [
  {
    "@type": "erdif:LocalIdentifier",
    "registry": "RUIAN",
    "registryCountry": "CZ",
    "registryLevel": "Address",
    "identifier": "22349811"
  }
],

  "streetAddress": "Korunní 810/104",

}

docs.title: Language maps
docs.text:
Text intended for people is written as a key–value map whose keys are ISO 639-1 language codes. In the context these properties are declared with @container: "@language".

"description": {
  "cs": "Prostorný byt 2+kk v cihlovém domě po rekonstrukci.",
  "en": "Spacious two-room apartment in a renovated brick building."
}

docs.title: Codelist values
docs.text: Codelist values are not translated. The English PascalCase identifier is always transmitted; translating it into the user's language is the client's responsibility. The labels in each codelist are language maps as well, so clients can look up a translation there.

docs.title: Context declaration
docs.text:
All terms of the format are defined in the JSON-LD context schema/context.jsonld, published at https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1/context.jsonld. A document references it in its @context key:

{
  "@context": "https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1/context.jsonld",
  ...
}
Prefix IRI Description (default) https://schema.org/ @vocab — default vocabulary erdif https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1# Custom extension for European specifics erdif-cl https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/codelist/v1/ Codelist values xsd http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema# Literal datatypes

The context declares every term of the format explicitly, including the ones reused from schema.org and the properties of nested schema.org types (QuantitativeValue, GeoCoordinates, PostalAddress). Numeric, boolean and date values are coerced to the matching XSD datatype, so expansion produces typed literals. The context is @protected, so a document cannot redefine a term of the format in its own inline context.

Terms that schema.org already defines with a matching meaning (for example price, floorSize, geo, yearBuilt) are reused. Everything else is defined in erdif: and listed in the vocabulary.

docs.title: RDFS/OWL vocabulary
docs.text:
Next to the JSON-LD context, the same terms are published as an RDFS/OWL vocabulary in Turtle at https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1/erdif.ttl (docs/ns/v1/erdif.ttl). It declares every class as owl:Class with its schema.org superclass, every erdif: property with domain and range, the reused schema.org properties with schema:domainIncludes, and every codelist as a skos:ConceptScheme with its values as skos:Concept. Cardinalities are not part of the vocabulary; they belong to the JSON Schemas and to application profiles. The file is meant for linked-data tooling, for example as a vocabulary import into Dataspecer. It is generated by scripts/build_vocabulary.py from the term registry and the codelists and must not be edited by hand.

Namespace IRIs contain only the major version (v1). Backward-compatible changes keep the IRIs; a breaking change introduces v2. See Versioning.

docs.title: Codelist values
docs.text:
A codelist property is written with a short code, but expands to a full IRI thanks to a scoped context:

"transactionType": "Sale"

expands to

https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/codelist/v1/TransactionType#Sale

Developers work with readable codes, while linked-data consumers get an unambiguous identifier of the value.

docs.title: Multiple typing rule
docs.text:
Every entity carries two types at once:

  • a schema.org type, which makes the data understandable to search engines, AI agents and any generic schema.org consumer,
  • an erdif: type, which carries the domain semantics of ERDIF and is what ERDIF validation relies on.
"@type": ["RealEstateListing", "erdif:Advert"]
"@type": ["PriceSpecification", "erdif:Price"]
"@type": ["Room", "erdif:Room"]

Where schema.org offers a more specific subtype (Apartment instead of Accommodation, ImageObject instead of MediaObject), producers should use it. Entities without a suitable schema.org counterpart (for example erdif:Building, erdif:Parking) carry only the erdif: type.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: ERDIF distinguishes two things that both carry a version: the specification and the documents created according to it.

docs.title: Specification version
docs.text:
The specification follows Semantic Versioning:

Change Version bump Examples Breaking major (2.0.0) removing or renaming a property, changing a cardinality from optional to required, removing a codelist value Backward compatible minor (1.1.0) adding an optional property, a class or a codelist value Editorial patch (1.0.1) clarifying documentation, fixing typos

Every release is a git tag (v1.0.0, v1.0.0-beta.1). The documentation site keeps each major version side by side (v1, v2) together with the dev version built from the main branch; use the version switcher in the header to change between them. All changes are listed in the Changelog.

Pre-release versions (1.0.0-beta.1) may change in any way before the final release.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Namespace IRIs contain only the major version:

https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/ns/v1#
https://erdif-org.github.io/erdif-spec/codelist/v1/

Minor and patch releases only add terms, so the IRIs stay the same and existing data keep their meaning. A major release introduces new IRIs (/ns/v2#), so data created against different major versions never mix silently.

docs.title: Document version
docs.text:
Every document states the specification version it was created against in formatVersion on the root Advert:

"formatVersion": "1.0.0-beta.1"

The value is the full specification version, including any pre-release label.

A consumer:

  • must reject a document whose major version it does not support,
  • should accept a document with a newer minor or patch version of a supported major version and ignore properties it does not know,
  • may use the full version for diagnostics and statistics.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Advert is the root entity of every ERDIF document and represents one offer of a property on the market. It carries the commercial part of the offer — transaction type, prices, marketing text, media and the contact — while the physical property is described separately in Realty.

This split reflects the fact that one property can be offered repeatedly and in different ways over time (sold, later rented out), whereas its physical description stays the same.

The marketing text (description) belongs to the advert, not to the property: it is written for one specific offer and changes with the transaction type.

The entity is typed as schema:RealEstateListing, which makes the document understandable to search engines and generic schema.org consumers, and as erdif:Advert, which carries the ERDIF semantics.

docs.text:
Entity types: schema:RealEstateListing + erdif:Advert

Root entity of the format. Represents a single real estate offer.

At least one language is required. Written as a language map. contact erdif:contact erdif:Contact 1 Contact entity managing the offer. realty erdif:realty erdif:Realty 1 Physical property the offer concerns. prices erdif:price erdif:Price 1..* Price items of the offer. media erdif:media erdif:Media 0..* Photos, videos, floor plans and virtual tours. exportInformation erdif:exportInformation erdif:ExportInformation 1 Export audit trail.

    "en": "Spacious two-room apartment in a renovated brick building."
  },
  "prices": [ ... ],
  "contact": { ... },
  "realty": { ... },
  "media": [ ... ],
  "exportInformation": { ... }

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Building describes the building a property belongs to. An apartment is one of many units in a building, and attributes such as the construction type, the year of completion or the presence of an elevator are shared by all of them. Keeping them in a separate entity avoids mixing building-level facts with the description of the unit.

For a house the building and the property are the same object; the building attributes are still written into building, so consumers find them in one place regardless of the property type. Land parcels have no building.

The year of completion reuses schema:yearBuilt. schema.org has no properties for the other attributes, so they are defined in erdif:.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Entity types: erdif:Building

The building the property belongs to. Its attributes are shared by all units in the building, so they are kept apart from the unit itself.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Contact describes the party managing the offer — an agent, a real estate office or the owner advertising directly.

The entity is typed as erdif:Contact together with a schema.org type. Producers use schema:Person or schema:Organization, or any of their subtypes (for example RealEstateAgent).

docs.title: Separation of personal data
docs.text:
A contact usually carries personal data of a natural person (name, e-mail, phone number). Under the GDPR such data must be removable or anonymisable independently of the rest of the offer.

ERDIF therefore keeps the contact in a separate entity with no property data mixed in. A receiving system can:

  • store the contact apart from the property and the advert,
  • delete or anonymise it on request without touching the offer itself,
  • keep publishing the offer with a replacement contact (e.g. the office).

docs.text:

  "contactType": "Agent",

  "telephone": "+420123456789"

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Equipment is an item of furnishing or equipment. It is bound to a specific room rather than to the property as a whole, so the information where the item is located is preserved (a dishwasher in the kitchen, a washing machine in the bathroom).

The category comes from the EquipmentType codelist; the optional name is a language map with a human-readable label.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
ExportInformation is the audit trail of the export: which system produced the data, under which identifier the advert is known there, and when the export happened.

It lets a receiving system match records on repeated imports — the pair sourceSystem + sourceAdvertId identifies the same advert across exports — and decide, using exportedAt, whether an incoming document is newer than the stored one.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
InspireIdentifier references a spatial object published under the EU INSPIRE directive. INSPIRE data are available in every member state with the same structure, so this identifier is the primary supranational way to locate a property: it resolves to the exact spatial object (address point, building or cadastral parcel) and, through it, to the national address.

The identifier follows the INSPIRE structure: a theme, the namespace of the data provider and a local identifier within that namespace. Supported themes:

Theme Spatial object AD Address point BU Building CP Cadastral parcel

docs.text:

  "theme": "AD",
  "namespace": "CZ.CUZK.AD",
  "localId": "26777598"

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
LocalArea describes one amenity in the surroundings of the property — a public transport stop, a school, a kindergarten, a park, a shop and so on — optionally with its name and distance from the property.

The surroundings are attached to Realty, not to Location. The location identifies where the property is; the surroundings describe what is nearby, which is descriptive information used for presentation and search, not for spatial identification.

schema.org has no property for nearby places, so the link is erdif:localArea. For the amenity itself, however, schema.org offers specific types (BusStop, SubwayStation, Preschool, School, Park, Hospital, ...), and producers are encouraged to use them next to Place.

docs.text:

  {
    "@type": ["SubwayStation", "erdif:LocalArea"],
    "amenityType": "MetroStation",
    "name": { "cs": "Náměstí Míru" },
    "distance": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 350, "unitCode": "MTR" }
  },
  {
    "@type": ["Preschool", "erdif:LocalArea"],
    "amenityType": "Kindergarten",
    "distance": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 200, "unitCode": "MTR" }
  }
]

docs.text:
LocalIdentifier carries an identifier from a national registry, such as the Czech RÚIAN. National identifiers play no role in locating the property at the European level; they are passed through unchanged so that the end user or a local system can verify the property in the national registry.

A location may carry several local identifiers, for example one for the address and one for the building.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Location identifies where the property is. It combines three independent means of identification, described in detail in Geolocation:

  1. an INSPIRE identifier (InspireIdentifier) as the primary supranational reference,
  2. WGS 84 coordinates as a mandatory fallback, because an INSPIRE identifier may not exist yet (e.g. for new buildings),
  3. national identifiers (LocalIdentifier) and a postal address as supplementary information.

Coordinates are often deliberately shifted to protect the exact address. The approximateCoordinates flag makes this explicit, so a consumer knows whether the point can be used for precise map display.

Information about the surroundings is not part of the location; it is modelled separately as LocalArea.

The entity is typed as schema:Place and erdif:Location.

docs.text:

Property Semantics Range Cardinality Description globalIdentifier erdif:globalIdentifier erdif:InspireIdentifier 0..1 Supranational INSPIRE spatial identifier. geo schema:geo schema:GeoCoordinates 1 WGS 84 coordinates. Mandatory fallback. approximateCoordinates erdif:approximateCoordinates xsd:boolean 1 Flag indicating whether coordinates are approximate. localIdentifiers erdif:localIdentifier erdif:LocalIdentifier 0..* National registry identifiers (e.g. RUIAN). address schema:address schema:PostalAddress 0..1 Postal address in local format.

  "@type": ["Place", "erdif:Location"],
  "globalIdentifier": {
    "@type": "erdif:InspireIdentifier",
    "theme": "AD",
    "namespace": "CZ.CUZK.AD",
    "localId": "26777598"
  },
  "geo": { "@type": "GeoCoordinates", "latitude": 50.07553, "longitude": 14.43781 },
  "approximateCoordinates": false,
  "localIdentifiers": [ ... ],
  "address": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "Korunní 810/104",
    "addressLocality": "Praha",

    "addressCountry": "CZ"
  }

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Media is one multimedia item of the offer — a photo, a video, a floor plan or a virtual tour — referenced by URL. The optional position defines the display order.

The caption is a language map, like every other text meant for people in the format. A portal that presents an offer in several languages can then show the caption in the same language as the rest of the advert, instead of falling back to the language of the producer.

The entity is typed as schema:MediaObject or one of its subtypes (for example ImageObject, VideoObject) and as erdif:Media.

docs.text:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Parking describes a parking option that belongs to the property — an outdoor space, a covered space, a space in a shared garage or a private garage — with the number of spaces and whether it is included in the price.

Parking is not modelled as a room: it does not count towards the layout or usable area of the unit, and a space in a shared garage is not part of the unit at all.

When parking is paid separately (includedInPrice: false), its price is given as a regular price item with priceType Parking. A garage or parking space offered on its own uses realtyType Parking and is described by the same entity.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A Price is a single price item of an offer. An advert carries one or more price items, each with its own type, amount, currency and — for periodic payments — unit. This lets an offer state, for example, the rent together with service charges, a deposit and the price of a parking space, without a dedicated property for each of them.

The currency is an ISO 4217 code and the unit a UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 code (MON per month, ANN per year, MTK per m²).

When the seller does not publish the amount, price is omitted and priceOnRequest is set to true.

The entity is typed as schema:PriceSpecification and erdif:Price.

docs.text:

May be omitted only when priceOnRequest is true. priceOnRequest erdif:priceOnRequest xsd:boolean 0..1 Flag indicating that the price is available on request only. priceCurrency schema:priceCurrency xsd:string 1 Currency per ISO 4217. unitCode schema:unitCode xsd:string 0..1 Unit of measure per UN/CEFACT (e.g. MON per month, MTK per sqm). negotiable erdif:negotiable xsd:boolean 0..1 Flag indicating whether the price is negotiable.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
• price-or-on-request — Each price item must contain either price, or priceOnRequest set to true.
  • periodic-price-unit — When priceType is Rent or ServiceCharges, unitCode is required (e.g. MON per month, ANN per year).
  • parking-price — A price item with priceType Parking should be present when any parking option of the realty has includedInPrice set to false.

    "negotiable": true
  },
  {
    "@type": ["PriceSpecification", "erdif:Price"],
    "priceType": "ServiceCharges",
    "price": 3400,
    "priceCurrency": "CZK",
    "unitCode": "MON"
  }
]

  "@type": ["PriceSpecification", "erdif:Price"],

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Realty describes the physical property independently of how it is currently being offered. It holds the internationally comparable core — type of property and area — together with ownership, energy class, condition and the links to its location, building, rooms, utilities, parking and surroundings.

The area follows the type of property: buildings and units state floorSize, land parcels state plotSize. Either way the area is given in square metres (MTK), which satisfies the mandatory core of the format.

Attributes of the whole building (construction, year built, elevator) are not stored here but in Building, because all units of a building share them. Accessibility is split by level: features of the property as a whole (entrance, access to the unit) are stated here, features of a specific room (bathroom, turning space) on the room.

The entity is typed as erdif:Realty together with schema:Accommodation or one of its subtypes (for example Apartment, House). Land parcels are not accommodation and use schema:Place instead.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
• realty-area — floorSize is required unless realtyType is Land; plotSize is required when realtyType is Land. This satisfies the mandatory area of the international core.
  • land-has-no-rooms — When realtyType is Land, rooms must be absent or empty.
  • accessibility-level — Values of accessibility must be applicable to the property level (appliesTo contains Realty in the AccessibilityFeature codelist).
  • land-has-no-building — When realtyType is Land, building and floorLevel must be absent.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
"realty": {
  "@type": ["Apartment", "erdif:Realty"],
  "realtyType": "Apartment",
  "ownershipType": "Personal",
  "energyClass": "C",
  "condition": "AfterRenovation",
  "floorSize": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 58.4, "unitCode": "MTK" },
  "floorLevel": 3,
  "accessibility": ["ElevatorAccess"],
  "building": { ... },
  "location": { ... },
  "rooms": [ ... ],
  "utilityNetworks": [ ... ],
  "parking": [ ... ],
  "localArea": [ ... ]
}

A land parcel has no rooms and no building:

"realty": {
  "@type": ["Place", "erdif:Realty"],
  "realtyType": "Land",
  "plotSize": { "@type": "QuantitativeValue", "value": 1250, "unitCode": "MTK" },
  "location": { ... }
}

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Room describes one room of the property. The list of rooms replaces country-specific layout notations (such as the Czech "2+kk"): a consumer can derive the layout and the total usable area from the room types and sizes in any local convention.

Rooms are optional (0..*): every building has at least one room, land parcels have none. Parking spaces are not rooms — they are described by Parking, because they do not count towards the layout or usable area.

Accessibility features that concern a specific room (walk-in shower, grab bars, turning space for a wheelchair) are stated on the room; features of the property as a whole are stated on Realty.

The entity is typed as schema:Room and erdif:Room.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
UtilityNetwork states how the property is connected to one utility network. The network (water, sewage, electricity, heating, cooling, gas, telecom, internet) and the means of connection (public mains, private well, septic tank, ...) are two independent axes, so they are expressed by two properties with two codelists.

Which connections belong to which network is defined machine-readably by appliesTo in the UtilityConnection codelist. A connection may belong to several networks: a reversible heat pump or air conditioning unit both heats and cools. Such a device is stated once per network, so that a consumer can ask for heating and for cooling separately.

The network is therefore not derivable from the connection, which is why both properties are always given.
